## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

`lock-diff.sh` shows `nix-devshell` bumped (plus its sub-inputs `devenv_2`,
`home-manager_2`, `llm-agents`), `mcp-servers-nix` dropped entirely. The
only `flake.modules.*` consumer of the `nix-devshell` input, per
`consumers.sh nix-devshell`, is `hermes` (via `mcp-overlay.nix`,
`groot-hm.nix`, `llm-agents-overlay.nix`). The `nixos-tools` gateway repoint
(06f23c3) lives in `modules/flake/checks.nix`, which sets
`devenv.shells.default`/`checks.pre-commit-check` via `perSystem` — it
registers no `flake.modules.nixos`/`homeManager` key, so `consumers.sh`
correctly finds no host reaching it; it is zero-drift by construction, not
assumption.

The devshell-function commit (04812e6) is the one that needed checking
rather than assuming. It edits `lib/shell-aliases.nix`,
`modules/user/bash.nix`, and `modules/user/fish.nix`. `consumers.sh
user-bash` and `consumers.sh user-fish` both resolve to every fleet
host — `sweet16`, `petunia`, `avina`, `hermes` (NixOS, via each host's
`home.nix`/`groot-hm.nix`) plus `dualie`, `forge`, `rk3588` (standalone HM).
These are not hermes-only or zero-drift modules; they are fleet-wide
Home Manager registry keys.

Corrected expected-drift set: **sweet16, petunia, avina, hermes, groot@dualie,
groot@forge** all drift (devenv-devshell alias removed, equivalent bash/fish
function added — same default behavior, different generated shell-rc text).
**groot@rk3588** is architecture-N/A, excluded per `validation.md`. No
config is expected to show zero drift.

### Actual vs expected

`verify-drift.sh` reports DRIFT on exactly `sweet16, petunia, avina,
hermes, groot@dualie, groot@forge`, and `N/A` on `groot@rk3588`. This is
the full corrected expected-drift set, with no extra and no missing
entries — sets are equal.

The task briefing's initial expectation (hermes-only drift) was wrong: it
assumed `modules/flake/checks.nix` and the user shell-alias modules were
zero-drift by construction without checking what consumes them. Checking
with `consumers.sh` showed `checks.nix` registers no registry key (true
zero-drift) but `user-bash`/`user-fish` reach the entire fleet (real,
expected drift, just not the drift everyone assumed up front).

Spot-checked the `sweet16` drv diff (`nix show-derivation | python3 -m
json.tool`, pre vs post): the only differing inputs are `etc.drv` and
`activate.drv` (and their downstream output hashes) — kernel, firmware,
systemd, and all other inputs are byte-identical. This confirms the drift
is isolated to the `/etc` config text produced by the bash/fish module
change, not a stray package or input bump leaking in from elsewhere.
